newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate slides further to 9.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate slides further to 9.2 pct.

text.p: Croatian average money market rate continued its three-day slide on Friday, losing 60 basis points to 9.2 percent despite growing demand which dealers attributed to weekly tax payments
Settlements doubled to 67.9 million kuna, leaving some 20 million surplus on the supply side.
All but 8.6 million kuna were fresh borrowings, mostly call money charged at unchanged 8.0 percent, after falling from about 10 percent last week.
Insurers rolled over old call-money borrowings at a steady nine percent rate while two-week and one-month money was issued at 12 and 13.5 percent respectively.
Bankers charged 15 and 16 percent for old two- and four-week money to savings banks which payed 18 percent for two-month deals. Monthly interbank money was rolled ower at 13-13.5 percent rates.
Central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Saturday and Sunday slightly weaker at 6.1665 versus the dollar and at 3.5700 against the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
